units.title: Physical Fitness, Wellness & Lifestyle
units.topics: • Meaning & Importance: Understanding the significance of maintaining physical fitness and wellness for overall health and quality of life. • Components of Physical Fitness: o Cardiovascular Endurance: The ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen during sustained physical activity. o Muscular Strength: The maximum amount of force a muscle or group of muscles can generate. o Muscular Endurance: The ability of a muscle to continue to perform without fatigue. o Flexibility: The range of motion available at a joint. o Body Composition: The proportion of fat and non-fat mass in the body. ## p40 • Components of Wellness: o Physical Wellness: Regular physical activity and proper nutrition. o Emotional Wellness: Understanding and managing feelings. o Social Wellness: Developing a sense of connection and belonging. o Intellectual Wellness: Engaging in creative and stimulating mental activities. o Spiritual Wellness: Seeking meaning and purpose in human existence.

units.title: Yoga
units.topics: • Meaning & Importance: Yoga is a mind-body practice that combines physical postures, breathing exercises, and meditation to promote overall health and well-being. • Elements of Yoga: o Asanas: Physical postures that improve flexibility, strength, and balance. o Pranayama: Breathing techniques that enhance respiratory function and mental clarity. o Meditation: Mental exercises that promote relaxation and mindfulness. • Introduction to Key Asanas: o Sukhasana: Easy Pose, promotes relaxation and meditation. o Tadasana: Mountain Pose, improves posture and balance. o Padmasana: Lotus Pose, enhances meditation and flexibility. o Shashankasana: Rabbit Pose, stretches the spine and calms the mind. o Naukasana: Boat Pose, strengthens the core and improves digestion. o Vrikshasana: Tree Pose, enhances balance and concentration. o Garudasana: Eagle Pose, improves focus and balance

units.title: ntroduction to Human Rights and Duties
units.topics: • Human Values: Understanding the significance of dignity, liberty, equality, justice, unity in diversity, ethics, and morals. • Human Rights Education: Meaning and importance of educating individuals on human rights to foster a just society. • Rights and Duties: The interrelationship between inherent, inalienable, and universal rights for individuals and groups, and the corresponding duties.

units.title: Legal Instruments and Terminology
units.topics: • Legal Instruments: Definition and significance of binding legal instruments such as covenants, charters, declarations, treaties, conventions, protocols, executive orders, and statutes. ## p42 • International Law: Understanding the role of various legal documents in enforcing human rights.

units.title: United Nations and Human Rights
units.topics: • History of Human Rights: A brief history of human rights from international and national perspectives. • UN Provisions: Overview of the United Nations Charter and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, covering civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights, and duties and limitations. • Final Provisions: A look at the final provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

units.title: Community Art Initiatives and Public Art Projects
units.topics: • Objective: Investigate how art engages with communities through public installations and collaborative projects. • Focus Areas: o Study of murals, street art, and community-driven art initiatives. o Analysis of the impact of public art on community identity and social issues. o Documentation of the processes involved in planning and executing public art projects

units.title: Artist Residencies and Collaborative Workshops
units.topics: • Objective: Explore opportunities for artistic growth through residencies and collaborative environments. • Focus Areas: o Research on national and international artist residency programs. o Examination of the benefits and challenges of collaborative art-making. o Interviews or case studies of artists who have participated in residencies or workshops

units.title: Unit
units.topics: Digital Platforms and Virtual Exhibitions • Objective: Understand the role of digital media in contemporary art presentation and dissemination. • Focus Areas: o Study of online galleries, virtual exhibitions, and digital art fairs. o Evaluation of the accessibility and reach of digital platforms for artists and audiences. o Analysis of how digital tools are transforming traditional exhibition practices. ## p44

units.title: Digital Tools for Pictorial Composition
units.topics: • Introduction to digital painting software such as Adobe Photoshop, Corel Painter, and Procreate. • Understanding layers, brushes, and digital color palettes to create complex compositions. • Utilizing digital sketching techniques to plan and refine artwork.

units.title: ntegrating Traditional and Digital Media
units.topics: • Techniques for digitizing traditional artworks using scanners ## p45 and cameras. • Combining hand-drawn elements with digital enhancements to create mixed-media pieces. • Exploring the interplay between texture, form, and color in hybrid artworks.

units.title: Digital Presentation and Portfolio Development
units.topics: • Preparing digital files for various outputs, including print and web. • Designing digital portfolios that effectively showcase artistic skills and concepts. • Understanding the basics of digital exhibition platforms and online galleries.
